prompt.adult: After the shipwreck, everyone escaped to land. According to 28:1, what was the island called?
prompt.child: Paul’s ship was wrecked, but everyone reached land safely. What island were they on?
prompt.teen: Acts 28:1: “they then found out that the island was called” what?
prompt.older: According to Acts 28:1, what island did they reach after escaping the wreck?

verses.text: Now when they had escaped, they then found out that the island was called Malta.

explanation.child: Look at the last word of verse 1.
explanation.teen: 28:1 says they escaped and then names the island. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “the island was called” in 28:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 28:2 says the natives showed them unusual kindness and kindled a fire because of the rain and the cold.

prompt.adult: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire. According to 28:3, what came out because of the heat?
prompt.child: Paul put sticks on a fire, and something came out and fastened on his hand. What was it?
prompt.teen: Acts 28:3: what “came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand”?
prompt.older: According to Acts 28:3, what fastened on Paul’s hand?

verses.text: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

explanation.child: Look in the middle of verse 3.
explanation.teen: 28:3 says what Paul did, then what came out, then where it fastened. Read the middle.
explanation.older: It comes just before “came out because of the heat” in 28:3.

teaching.extended_explanation: 28:4 says the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand and thought he must be a murderer.
teaching.takeaway: A viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand.

prompt.adult: The commander said, “With a large sum I obtained this citizenship.” What did Paul say in reply in 22:28?
prompt.child: A Roman officer said he had paid a lot of money to become a Roman. How did Paul say he became one?
prompt.teen: Acts 22:28: Paul said, “But I was” what?
prompt.older: According to Acts 22:28, how did Paul hold his Roman citizenship?

verses.text: Then the commander came and said to him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He said, “Yes.”
The commander answered, “With a large sum I obtained this citizenship.” And Paul said, “But I was born a citizen.”

explanation.child: Look at Paul’s words at the end of verse 28.
explanation.teen: 22:27 has the question; 22:28 has the commander’s words, then Paul’s. Read Paul’s.

teaching.extended_explanation: 22:27 says the commander asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” and Paul said, “Yes.”
teaching.takeaway: Paul said, “But I was born a citizen.”

prompt.adult: Paul reasoned with Felix about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come. When did Felix say he would call for him, according to 24:25?
prompt.child: A governor became afraid while listening to Paul and sent him away. When did he say he would call Paul back?
prompt.teen: Acts 24:25: “Go away for now; when I have” what “I will call for you”?
prompt.older: According to Acts 24:25, when did Felix promise to call for Paul again?

verses.text: And after some days, when Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
Now as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was afraid and answered, “Go away for now; when I have a convenient time I will call for you.”

explanation.adult: Read the end of Felix’s words in 24:25.
explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 25.
explanation.teen: 24:24 says Felix came with Drusilla; 24:25 gives Paul’s subjects, Felix’s fear, then his words. Read the words.

teaching.extended_explanation: 24:24 says Felix sent for Paul and heard him. 24:25 says Felix was afraid.
teaching.takeaway: Felix said, “When I have a convenient time I will call for you.”

prompt.adult: In 25:19 Festus said Paul affirmed that a certain Jesus who had died was alive. In 26:24, what did Festus say was driving Paul mad?
prompt.child: As Paul made his defense, the governor shouted that he was out of his mind. What did he say was causing it?
prompt.teen: Acts 26:24: “Paul, you are beside yourself!” What “is driving you mad”?
prompt.older: Linking Acts 25:19 with 26:24, what did Festus blame for Paul’s words?

verses.text: but had some questions against him about their own religion and about a certain Jesus, who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
Now as he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are beside yourself! Much learning is driving you mad!”

explanation.adult: Read the end of Festus’ words in 26:24.
explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 26:24.
explanation.teen: 25:19 is Festus’ account; 26:24 has his loud words. Read the second sentence of them.
explanation.older: It comes just before “is driving you mad” in 26:24.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:19 says the questions were about their own religion. 26:25 says Paul answered that he spoke words of truth and reason.
teaching.takeaway: Festus said, “Much learning is driving you mad!”

verses.text: But the following night the Lord stood by him and said, “Be of good cheer, Paul; for as you have testified for Me in Jerusalem, so you must also bear witness at Rome.”
saying, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must be brought before Caesar; and indeed God has granted you all those who sail with you.’
